title: N-Queens
description:
A queen on a chessboard attacks every square in its row, in its column, and along both of its diagonals. The n-queens puzzle asks for n queens on an n by n board with no two of them attacking each other.

Implement a function called SolveNQueens that receives n and returns every distinct solution, in any order. A solution is a list of n strings, one per row from top to bottom. Each string has n characters: Q for a queen and . for an empty square.

SolveNQueens(4) -> [[".Q..", "...Q", "Q...", "..Q."], ["..Q.", "Q...", "...Q", ".Q.."]]
SolveNQueens(1) -> [["Q"]]

Some boards have no solution, and then the result is an empty list: SolveNQueens(2) -> [] and SolveNQueens(3) -> [].

A board that has already gone wrong must be abandoned as soon as the conflict appears, rather than being filled in and checked at the end. The hidden tests check this with n = 12, which has 14200 solutions and is far out of reach of trying every complete arrangement.
objective: Enumerate every placement of n non-attacking queens by backtracking, abandoning a partial board as soon as it has a conflict.
